title: dev.qory.run.exited
description: The run ended: the runtime exited, or the run was ended without one. The result of the run and its last event. Every run.exited contains state, how the run ended: succeeded, failed or cancelled, and Forager writes exit_code too, the runtime's exit status, -1 with gateway_lost and in every dev.qory.run.exited the gateway writes for a session's run. The schema fixes state to failed with gateway_lost, and exit_code to -1 when it is present, and does not require exit_code, so records written before, of runs with no process, still validate. The gateway's dev.qory.run.exited of a session's run that it ends has exit_code -1, and the state of its ending, the README's §The events, How a run ends; the session's own record of the code of the gateway's 410 has the runtime's exit status, so the schema fixes neither for those reasons.

state.description: How the run ended, on every run.exited. succeeded: the run ended well; failed: it ended badly; cancelled: it was stopped before it said how it went. A session's runtime that exits by itself is succeeded on exit status 0 and failed otherwise, a signal included. Forager's own endings: cancelled with timeout and interrupted; failed with session_lost, gateway_lost and batch_refused.

exit_code.description: The runtime's exit status, or -1 when it was killed by a signal, and -1 when the gateway ends a session's run, which holds no exit status of the runtime's. Forager writes it on every run.exited; records written before may lack it.

signal.description: The signal that killed the runtime, when one did: SIGKILL, SIGTERM.

reason.description: Why the run ended, when it ended other than by the runtime's own exit, or the reason its starter gave: an open code, a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and _, up to 64 characters. Forager's own codes are reserved: timeout, interrupted, stopped, session_lost, gateway_lost, batch_refused and run_closed; and so are the old names quiet, credential_expired, credential_check_unreachable, credential_check_invalid, run_ended_at_issuer, issuer_unreachable and issuer_answer_invalid, which Forager never writes, kept so that records written before still validate. Any other code is the starter's, carried as given; a starter's reason that equals a reserved code, or that is not a code, is dropped, and the run has no reason, its outcome kept. timeout: the run's time limit was reached and the session stopped the runtime. interrupted: the session's run was stopped from where it was started, a Ctrl-C or a signal to the program that runs the session, before the session observed the runtime's exit; exit_code and signal are the runtime's. stopped: the code of a gateway's 410 on the link, which the session records in its own record alone, failed when the 410 carries no state. session_lost: the gateway heard nothing from the session for 3 × its heartbeat interval. gateway_lost: the gateway was lost before the runtime's exit was recorded, because Forager died, and the event is written after the run has ended, by whatever sends the record again; duration_ms runs to the last event recorded. batch_refused: the gateway refused a batch of the session's (§The gateway's link); the gateway writes it in its record, and the session in its own. The session writes timeout and interrupted, and posts them; in its own record alone it records the reason of the gateway's 410, and run_closed, the gateway's 410 to a run already ended there, after the session's final event or when the gateway stops, which no other record holds. The resend of a record writes gateway_lost, and the gateway session_lost and batch_refused. A session's batch on the link carries no reason of Forager's but timeout and interrupted, and no reason of the starter's. Absent when the runtime ended by itself, and when it was stopped from outside Forager.

quiet_seconds.description: A quiet period in seconds, which Forager no longer writes: present only with the old reason quiet, in records written before, and absent otherwise.

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds from run.started to the run's end.
